sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads React, the keyboard and close icons, and the app data store.
sections.why: Needed to listen for keys, draw the panel, and change tabs.

sections.name: KeyboardShortcutsModal (part 1)
sections.title: Number key tab shortcuts
sections.what: Listens for key presses, skips text boxes, and maps keys 1 to 7 to the matching main tab. When open, draws the panel header.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the shortcut behaviour and its panel together in one component.
sections.watch_out: Ctrl or Cmd with a number also changes tabs.

sections.name: KeyboardShortcutsModal (part 2)
sections.title: Shortcut list and close button
sections.what: Lists each shortcut with its key and description, and gives a close button in the footer. Closing sets the open flag to false.
sections.why: Likely reason: a readable reference the user can check at any time.
sections.watch_out: The Escape entry says any modal closes with Escape, but Escape handling is not in this file.

summary: Hotkey panel that lists the keyboard shortcuts, plus a listener that lets the number keys 1 to 7 jump to the main tabs.
purpose: Lets users move around the app quickly and shows them which shortcuts exist.
why: Likely reason: a shortcut list is only useful if users can find it. The reason for the number order is not stated in the code.
how: Always listens for key presses. Ignores keys typed into text boxes. A number key from 1 to 7 switches to the matching tab. When the open flag is set, draws the panel with the shortcut list and a close button.
inputs: Key presses, the open flag, and the tab action from the store.
outputs: Tab changes when number keys are pressed, and the shortcut panel when it is open.
risks: The listener does not check Ctrl or Cmd, so Ctrl plus a number also changes tabs. The label list is separate from the tab order and could drift out of step with it. The Escape line promises that Escape closes any modal, but this file does not handle Escape.
debug: If a number key opens the wrong tab, compare the tab order with the label order. If number keys trigger while typing, check the text box check. If the panel never opens, check whether anything sets the open flag to true.
